restrictions: The two messages have 55 and 63 bytes: each is one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and its true block length; the 63-byte message ends in eight zero bytes, so that in the zero-filled block of both messages the words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every choice of eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, and one of the eight words is the round-1 state word Y4, which the search holds inside a sub-class of 131,072 values, a quarter of the class of 524,288 values of entry c66f230d of the same participant. Heuristic part: a search over 2^100.534 such pairs for one whose remaining 128 digest bits agree. The search works on batches of seven pairs and examines a batch further only if one of its pairs passes a filter on one internal word (rule A, eight bit conditions); rule A is not implied by a collision, and a pair that fails it is examined further only if another pair of its batch passes, and is not counted in the success bound.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; seven trials per 256-bit word in 36-bit lanes on a 16-register load/store machine on which every memory word costs one load each time it is fetched, except nine words kept in registers during a loop. A word runs stage A, 37 operations plus 10 loads; only a word in which a trial passes rule A runs stage 2, 105 plus 30. With the neighbour path of proof.md 6.7, the routing between pieces stored and loaded, and the middle steps, the table build and the outer step, a trial-equivalent is charged 1.65 operations, an upper bound. No sorting, no lookup by value and no table that grows with the number of trials. The algorithm halts with failure when E representative words (one in 32) or S neighbour words have run stage 2, when G representatives have opened their gate, when W neighbour words have run stage A, or when 2^84 trials that passed the second test have been processed (proof.md 6.4, step 4).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1 to H6. The factor 92,675,904 in H1 is assumed and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments; with the uniform rate instead, the same search needs 2^127 trials and gives time_log2 119.0. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed. The loops of the search, their ranges and the processing of a trial that passes the second test are defined in proof.md; the submitted program contains and counts their pieces, not the loops.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, two bits of the sub-class and three 32-bit constants of the rule test are stored in the program (48 bytes of advice). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count; the sub-class and rule A were proposed by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) from exact counts that the participant's counter reproduces. preprocessing_log2 80 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 9: every search runs over a stated range and every program run halts at a stated cap, so its cost, fewer than 2^88.45 operations, is a bound by construction whatever the programs return. That it returns the stored constants rests on the participant's solver log and counts; its steps for the sub-class, the rule and the flips have not been run. Choosing a sub-class from the rate of every member follows winglock (2125212, 2bb5d604). memory_log2_bytes 35 bounds that procedure and the search (below 2^26 bytes). No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the 2^100.534 enumerated trials behave, with respect to the event that the 128-bit residual R is zero and the trial satisfies rule A, like independent events of probability at least 92,675,904 * 2^-128 each, to the extent that the probability that no trial has this event is at most exp(-1/2) + 0.001. The assumption has two parts, a rate and the absence of clustering, and neither follows from the other.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 6.4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values defined by eta = 830303cf and by bits 21 and 26 of e1 (Lemmas Q and Q2), contexts of seven words of which four come from the random word, one (C0.d1) runs over 1,184,670 values and two (w5 and X2) over all 2^32 values, and all members of the sub-class for every context. Rule A is the set of eight bit conditions of Section 6.3 on the word h1 of a trial (Lemma A).
heuristics.extrapolation: From a participant count, in integer arithmetic, of the rate of the sub-class under the seven-word model, that is of the number of solutions with Y4 in the sub-class of the seven-word system that determines R: for each value beta of an auxiliary difference of one of the two calls, every outcome of that call is enumerated, the other call is counted exactly for it, split by rule A, and the probability of the outcome is counted exactly. Over the 60 values of beta that have a part for the whole class the count is 185,377,197.55 times the uniform expectation (53 values and 317 outcomes with a part); 185,358,111.47 of it satisfies rule A; the claim uses 185,355,453.45, the sum over the 99 outcomes in which every solution satisfies rule A. The sub-class and the rule were proposed by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) with a counter of its own; its exact fractions for the totals, the rule masses, every value of beta and 3,243 integers on 1,081 outcomes (three per outcome) are equal to the participant's; the recount was made with its figures at hand, and the figure that the claim uses is the participant's alone. From checks of the counter: complete enumeration with 8-bit words including sub-classes and three-bit parities (6,805,032 integers, none different); two functions for the split by the rule that agree on 687 outcomes. From comparisons of the model with real trials at 32 bits in the loop order of this package, for the whole class and other rules: averaged over outer tuples, events of one call down to a probability of about 2^-40 agree with the model (listed E1 outcomes: 138 against 152.0 expected); in the order of entry c66f230d, 24 runs of 2^45 real trials on another machine: 692 against 690.78. From scaled-down end-to-end runs with 8-bit and 10-bit words in this loop order, without sub-class and rule: 470 collisions against 467.6 predicted in 436 runs (the first 92 runs were low, 56 against 74.8, and the later ones were made because of that), and in a larger job of 8,448 runs with expectations written down beforehand 8,108 against 8,313.6 (-2.25 standard deviations: 3.3 percent low with 8-bit words, level with 10-bit words); and in the order of entry c66f230d: 345 against 335.76 in a plan fixed beforehand. All in proof.md Section 10. The factor and the absence of clustering are assumptions; the count is what the factor is set against, not a measurement of the trials, and none of these measurements reaches the joint event (R = 0 and rule A) over the real trials of a run that H1 asks about.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 92,675,904 is assumed. It is set against a participant count of 185,355,453, 2.00 times larger, which the organizer-run experiments do not measure; the success bound needs a factor of at least 92,379,824. With factor 1 (the uniform rate) the claim would be 2^127 trials and time_log2 119.0. The count is exact only under the seven-word model, that six of the seven words behave like independent uniform words over the trials; that the trials of the algorithm meet the counted solutions at the model's rate is the assumption, and so is the absence of clustering, which the model does not address. The model does NOT hold inside one context for rule A (single contexts have between 0.0071 and 0.0421 of their batches entering stage 2 where the average is 0.02617) and NOT inside one outer step for the call E1 (the rate of single events of E1 was seen between 0.02 and 2 times its average from one outer tuple to another); only averages over outer steps have the model's values, and whether the rate of trials that satisfy rule A and have R = 0 has the model's value on average was not measured and cannot be. One count of the layout runs is unexplained (3 events where 14.65 are expected in one window of 2^44 trials). A graphics-card run now measures rule A in the sub-class (24 outer tuples, 2^44.59 real trials; rule A passes at 2^-8.000002 and a marker at 2^-32.2 is about 1.18 times richer in the sub-class than in the whole class, while its deeper marker at 2^-40.15 has 14 counts against 21.59 expected and settles nothing at that precision), and a scaled-down end-to-end run with the sub-class and an eight-condition rule finds collisions at the exact per-trial count (121 against 120.23); but no run reaches rule A together with an event of R, and neither measures the kept mass that H1 is set against (proof.md Section 10). The sub-class and the rule were chosen by the count: the sub-class gains a factor of 1.142 under the model, and no measurement on real messages shows that gain; a choice that is best under the model says nothing about the model. Rule A is not implied by a collision; that it loses only one part in 10,000 of the count inside the sub-class rests on the two counts, and on the whole class it would lose more than half. The count rests on few paths: four values of beta carry 98.8% of it. The list of 60 values of beta rests on uncertified solver answers and on the other model's enumeration. The counting programs are not in the package. All trials of a run share four seed words, the 2^49 trials of an outer step share six words and, for one member, a whole table row, and the 2^52.18 trials of a run with one value of w5 and one member share Y12 and w5; their independence is assumed. The loops, their ranges and the processing of passes are defined in the text and are not in the submitted program. The proofs of the new lemmas (T2, T3, T4, Q2 and Lemma A in its new form) and this whole text were written and checked by helper agents of the participant, instances of one AI model; three further helper agents reviewed the assembled text once, and their corrections and the evidence added after the review were not read again by them; no person has read it. Nothing here is organizer-verified except the two declared experiments, which do not measure the 128-bit rate and are not a test of H1.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than 2^84 of the trials of a run pass the 32-bit E1 test of proof.md Lemma N without having R = 0.
heuristics.scope: The E1 test of Section 6.3 on all trials of Section 6.4, whether or not their batch runs stage 2; the algorithm processes only the passes in batches that run stage 2, which are fewer. A pass rate of 2^-31.41 would give 2^70.03 passes; the budget corresponds to a pass rate of 2^-17.44 and is larger by a factor of more than 2^13.9, and processing 2^84 passes is charged in the time bound (2^94 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: From participant measurements of the pass rate on real trials with these constants at 32 bits in the loop order of this package, for the whole class of 524,288 values of Y4: 2^-31.41 per trial on average and 2^-31.20 in the outer tuple with the most (proof.md Section 10, layout runs), to the trials of one run, which have Y4 in the sub-class.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. For the sub-class the graphics-card run of Section 10 gives 9,537 passes of the E1 test in 2^44.585 trials, a rate of 2^-31.37. It is a mean; that the pass count of a full run, whose outer steps share four seed words, stays near that mean is assumed. The layout runs have random outer words and at most 2^26 values of X2 of one outer tuple. The cost of processing a pass, below 2^10 operations, is stated in words and was not written out on the counting machine. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H2 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than E of the representative words of a run hold a trial that satisfies rule A of proof.md Section 6.3, where E is the budget of Section 6.4, one in 32 of the representative words; so fewer than E representative words run stage 2. Neighbour words have their own budget (H6).
heuristics.scope: Rule A (Lemma A) on the trials of Section 6.4, in the seven-lane batches of Section 6.5. A batch runs stage 2 exactly when one of its seven trials satisfies rule A. The budget E is 2,341 * J / 256 rounded down, with J = 2^110 / 92,675,904 rounded up, times 64 / 41.02, rounded up, which is the constant RUN_PAIRS of the submitted program, 21,853,299,106,075,760,480,725,513 (proof.md Section 6.4, step 4); a run has at least J pairs of an outer step and a value of X2, one value of X2 in eight holds representatives, and it holds 2,341 representative words; E is one in 32 of the representative words of J pairs, the constant STAGE_2_BUDGET of the submitted program. The time bound charges stage 2 for that many representative words, and the algorithm halts with failure when the budget is reached. The statement is about the total over a run; it is not claimed context by context and is false for single contexts. It holds whenever fewer than E representatives of the run satisfy rule A, a share of 1.1430 times 2^-8 of the representatives.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the fact that a uniform 32-bit word satisfies the eight conditions of rule A with probability 2^-8, and from participant measurements on real trials of the sub-class at 32 bits on a processor: in 8,192 independent contexts with all members (2^30 trials) the share of the trials that satisfy rule A is 2^-8.0019 and the share of the batches that hold such a trial is 0.02617; in 512 outer steps with 16 values of X2 each, 2^-7.9992 and 0.02622, with the 512 outer steps between 0.0238 and 0.0289; with a second seed, 2^-8.0000 and 0.02622; against the budget 0.03125. For the whole class and the rules with four, five and six conditions, runs on a graphics card in the loop order of this package have the shares of the trials within one part in a million of 2^-4, 2^-5 and 2^-6 on average over outer tuples. All in proof.md Sections 6.5 and 10. The extrapolation is from these averages over sampled contexts to the average over the outer steps of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The share of the batches of ONE context that run stage 2 is not below the budget in every context: in the samples single contexts have between 0.0071 and 0.0421, and one whole value of X2 that was run in full has 0.0307. Only the average is below it, with room of 19 percent in these samples, which is less room than entry c66f230d had for its budget. That the average over the outer steps of one run, which share four seed words, stays below the budget is assumed; the cause of the dependence on the context is not analysed. Rule A with eight conditions is now recorded on a graphics card for the sub-class as well: of 2^44.59 real trials 103,079,088,429 pass it (2^-8.000002) and 0.026178 of the packed words enter stage 2, confirming the processor shares at 8,192 times the trials (proof.md Section 10). The outer words of these samples are random words; three samples of the review in the ranges of the algorithm give between 0.02617 and 0.02620. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H3 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005. The operation counts of the two stages are the submitted program's own, on a machine that keeps nine words in registers.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the number of neighbours found to satisfy rule A per representative, divided by the probability 2^-8 that a trial satisfies rule A, is at least 40.02 on the run as a whole, so that a representative yields at least 41.02 trial-equivalents on average over a run: one for itself and 40.02 for the neighbours its gate opens. H4 is a premise of the success probability of proof.md Section 7 and of the time bound of Section 8, which charges per trial-equivalent and divides the cost of a representative by 41.02.
heuristics.scope: The clusters of proof.md Section 6.7 on the trials of Section 6.4: a representative is a trial whose bits 14, 30 and 31 of e1 = Y3 + Y4 and of X2 are zero; its 63 neighbours are the trials reached by flipping a non-empty subset of those six bits, and they are examined only when the representative passes the gate, the four conditions of rule A that bits 0, 16 and 17 of h1 are zero and bit 1 is one. The statement is about the average over the representatives of a run; it is not claimed outer step by outer step and is false for single outer tuples, whose yields run from 15.9 to 57.1.
heuristics.extrapolation: From participant measurements on real messages of the sub-class, each with its own program and its own reference for the words of a trial: 40.018 +- 0.012 over 16,777,218 opened representatives, each on a fresh random outer tuple; 40.032 +- 0.075 and 40.056 +- 0.248 in two runs that enumerate all 16,384 representatives of a value of X2 in member order and then every trial of every cluster; 40.027 +- 0.010 by another AI model (Grok 4.7) with a program and a reference of its own; and 40.117 and 39.802 by a fourth agent over 4,096 and 128 outer steps. An opened cluster finds 2.5008 neighbours that satisfy rule A on average, and the gate opens for 0.0624630 of the representatives. All in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these averages over sampled outer tuples to the average over the outer steps of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The yield is a measured mean, not a count, and no bound for it exists. It depends on the outer tuple: the neighbours found per representative have a standard deviation of about 14 per cent between outer tuples, and single tuples run from 15.9 to 57.1 in yield (13.7 and 13.2 per cent, and 16.07 to 54.90, in the fourth agent's runs). Every run that measured it used random outer words rather than the walk of Section 6.4; that the average over the outer steps of one run, which share four seed words, is at least 40.02 is assumed. The six flips and the gate were chosen by measurement on a sampler, by a screen of 231,525 flip sets and a beam search, which tends to find a set that happens to look good; the chosen set was remeasured on larger samples by three programs, and another AI model's re-screen checks the screen, not the run. The claimed time is proportional to 1 / (1 + 40.02): a yield lower by one part in ten raises it by about 0.15. No run of the cluster procedure end to end with the gate carried to the neighbours as at full size exists (proof.md Section 10).

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the trials that the algorithm examines, the representatives and the neighbours of each representative whose gate opens, carry per trial at least the collision mass that rule A keeps on average over the whole sub-class, and the good trials of a run (R = 0 and rule A) do not come in clusters any more than H1 already allows; in particular the collisions of one cluster of 64 trials do not clump. H1 is read over the examined trials under this premise. H5 is a premise of the success probability of proof.md Section 7 and of the time bound of Section 8.
heuristics.scope: The trials examined by the cluster procedure of proof.md Sections 6.4 and 6.7 in one run, compared with the trials of the sub-class that satisfy rule A. The first part is about the collision mass of one examined trial, the second about the event that two trials of one cluster are both good. Trials of one cluster share their six outer words and differ in three bits of X2 and three bits of e1.
heuristics.extrapolation: First part: against the exact law of h1 in the sub-class, a decision diagram of 683,179 nodes from another AI model read by a helper agent with a reader of its own, the expected collision mass per examined trial divided by that per ordinary trial that satisfies rule A is 0.99950 +- 0.00036 on 1,325,033,143 clusters; a second agent measures 0.99994 +- 0.00006 on 1,032,096,571 examined trials; on a graphics card over 2^44.907 trials the first side over the 67 listed cells of beta and tau gives 1.0017 +- 0.0030, and 1.0000 on the four heaviest values of beta; GPT Sol 6.1 computed the factor exactly on three partial averages it could enumerate: 1.007971, 0.997446 and 1.000304. Second part: at the levels these tools reach the members of a cluster clump slightly negatively: a neighbour of a trial that satisfies rule A and carries one of the four heaviest values of beta carries one of them 0.9699 +- 0.0009 times as often as an independent trial, and Grok 4.7 measures the word of Lemma N zero on a neighbour, given zero on the representative, at 0.946 of the marginal rate at eight bits of agreement. All in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these proxies, at 2^-9, 2^-19 and about 2^-32, to the collision at about 2^-100.53.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. No measurement reaches the collision event. The first part is measured on proxies: its two sides must not be multiplied as independent factors, the other model says the factor for the whole ensemble is unknown and that a high retention of rule A does not imply that it is one, and the seven neighbours that flip only bits of X2 give 0.930 +- 0.059 on the 67 cells. The second part cannot be measured at full size: the collision has probability about 2^-100.53 per trial and the deepest events reached are about 2^-32 and 2^-40, so treating the measured clumping as a guide is an extrapolation over about 100 bits of conditioning; at twelve bits of agreement Grok 4.7 has 1.28 on only 11 events. A factor of ten at the level of tau would have shown in the counts; a factor of two would not. If an opened cluster fired as one trial, the claimed exponent would rise by about 1.32, and by 1.81 for 3.5 trials, most of the 2.2 that the clusters gain. Neither a reduced-word run end to end whose gate is carried to the neighbours at 0.6 to 0.87 as at full size, nor a proof that each of the six flipped bits still moves the collision given a collision at the representative, exists; the two scaled-down runs that exist carry the gate hardly (co-pass at most 0.41 against 0.25 by chance) and do not test this.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than G representatives of a run open their gate, fewer than W neighbour words of a run go through stage A and fewer than S neighbour words of a run enter stage 2, where G, W and S are the budgets of the neighbour path in step 4 of proof.md Section 6.4, each 1.2 times its measured mean per representative; so no budget of the neighbour path is reached.
heuristics.scope: The gate of proof.md Section 6.7 (bits 0, 16 and 17 of h1 zero and bit 1 one, four of the eight conditions of rule A) on the representatives of Section 6.4, the nine neighbour words that an opened gate sends through stage A, and those of them in which a trial satisfies rule A, which enter stage 2. The budgets are G = 1.2 * 0.0624630 * 2,048 * J, W = 1.2 * 0.5625 * 2,048 * J and S = 1.2 * 0.1364 * 2,048 * J, each rounded down, with J as defined in step 4 of Section 6.4 (the constant RUN_PAIRS of the submitted program); 2,048 * J is the number of representatives in J pairs of an outer step and a value of X2, one for each cluster of 64 trials. Section 8 charges the neighbour path at 1.2 times the measured means, and the algorithm halts with failure when one of the three budgets is reached. The statement is about the totals over a run; it is not claimed value of X2 by value of X2 and is false for single values of X2.
heuristics.extrapolation: From participant measurements on real messages of the sub-class over 256 random outer tuples with 32 random values of X2 each, every representative packed seven to a word in member order: the gate opens for 0.0624630 of the representatives, against 2^-4 = 0.0625 for a uniform h1; per representative 0.5625 neighbour words go through stage A (nine whenever the gate opens) and 0.1364 enter stage 2; three further programs reproduce each of these figures to within half a per cent (proof.md Section 10). The extrapolation is from these averages over sampled outer tuples and values of X2 to the average over the outer steps of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The budgets are 1.2 times measured means and are not proved. The count per value of X2 is not binomial: its variance is 11.18 times the binomial one pooled; single values of X2 have between 0.41 and 1.64 times the mean share of open gates, so single values of X2 exceed the budget, and the largest share seen for one value of X2 grows with the sample (1.64 times the mean over 8,192 values of X2, 1.72 over 16,384). Single outer tuples have between 0.058577 and 0.066032. That the average over the outer steps of one run, which share four seed words, stays below 1.2 times the measured means is assumed; the outer words of the samples are random words, not the walk of Section 6.4. If a budget were reached the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H6 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005.
